edits.headline: New York prosecutor reopens Cornell fraternity rape investigation
edits.subheadline: District Attorney Matthew Van Houten said his office would present evidence against seven fraternity members to a grand jury.
editorialBody: Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten reopened a criminal investigation into an alleged gang rape at Cornell University on Monday 28 September, the Associated Press and ABC News reported.
A former student sued on 16 September, saying seven members of the Chi Phi fraternity assaulted her in October 2024. The lawsuit also names Cornell, the AP reported.
Cornell said it supported the decision. "Any suggestion that the university did not impose consequential punishments for those involved is false," the university said.

Lovely Professional University in Phagwara, Punjab, suspended classes for 10 days from 28 September after a student protest turned violent, Business Today reported. Protesters set two police vehicles on fire.
The protest followed allegations that a student was raped on campus. The university called the allegations "false, baseless and fabricated".
The ship lost an engine shortly after launch, and the flight ended after 3 hours 9 minutes instead of the planned 10 hours, Satellite Today reported.
